title: Hook Framework for Content
subtitle: Your content is well-written and genuinely useful but it gets ignored. You're posting
useWhen: consistently and seeing minimal engagement. The problem isn't the content it's that nobody is stopping to read it.
howToUse: In a feed of infinite content, the first line of any post, email, or video is the only thing that decides whether the rest gets seen. A hook works by triggering one of four responses: Curiosity (I need to know how this ends), Relatability (that is exactly my situation), Controversy (I disagree and want to respond), or Value (this will help me right now). The 3H Hook System structures every piece of content around a strong opening that earns the scroll followed by a clear value delivery and a closing that creates engagement or action.
steps: Write 5 hook variations for every piece of content the best one is rarely the first.
Test different hook types across your audience: curiosity works on some, value on others.
The hook should be the last thing you write after you know what the content delivers.

If the hook doesn't make you want to keep reading, rewrite it before posting. The first line determines whether the rest gets read Curiosity Isn't a License to Bait A hook that promises one thing and delivers another earns a scroll-past on the next post, not the current one. Curiosity should point at the real value inside if the opening line and the content don't match, you're not hooking, you're baiting.
origin: Social media content strategy — Hook framework methodology, 2020s
promptBody:
Act as a content strategist and copywriter specialising in hooks.
Content topic     :  [WHAT THIS POST, EMAIL, OR VIDEO IS ABOUT]
Target audience :  [WHO WILL SEE THIS AND WHAT THEY CARE ABOUT]
Platform               :  [LINKEDIN / EMAIL / INSTAGRAM / YOUTUBE]
Core value            :  [WHAT THE READER WILL LEARN OR GET]
Write 5 hook variations using different hook types:
CURIOSITY HOOK         :  Creates a knowledge gap they must close
RELATABILITY HOOK   :  Opens with a situation they recognise
CONTROVERSY HOOK  :  Challenges a common belief in the space
VALUE HOOK                  :  Leads with the specific benefit upfront
STORY HOOK                  :  Opens mid-scene in a compelling moment
For each hook: write the opening line only (max 15 words).
Then recommend the strongest one for this audience.

proTip:
The curiosity hook is the most powerful but the most overused. The relatability hook is
the most underused  and often outperforms everything else because it makes the reader
feel seen before they've read a word of content. Start with: 'You know that moment
when...' and describe your audience's exact situation.
